Hi Emily / Samir —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick follow-up from our demo and the privacy/security items you flagged:

1) SOC 2: you asked for our SOC 2 Type II availability and evidence scope. I’ve attached a one-page summary (Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2027.pdf). Full report is available on request under NDA.

2) DPA + SCC: You mentioned procurement needs us to sign a DPA and indicate which SCC module we support. To make progress, could you confirm whether FinVera expects Redwood to be the data processor (standard for our hosted API) or if you will be treating Redwood as a joint-controller for certain data flows? We typically propose Processor + SCC Module 2 (Processor-to-Processor flow) for hosted API customers, but the right pick depends on:
- whether FinVera will send personal data for account admin/analytics only, or
- whether FinVera will provide data for model fine-tuning (that can change obligations).

3) Questionnaire / evidence: If you’d like, we can kick off the vendor security questionnaire in parallel. Who from your side should I assign the questionnaire to?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the expected controller/processor mapping for the use case described in the demo.
- I’ll share a short SCC module comparison and a draft DPA for legal review (attached).
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal sync this week.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx, SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2027.pdf

Soojin / Ben —

Thanks for the context. Below is a short legal note we can send directly to Emily and the FinVera counsel. I’ve also added inline suggestions to the draft DPA and a simple SCC comparison (see attached).

Short legal note (copy/paste friendly):

"Redwood Inference position — controller/processor and SCC module selection:

1) Controller / Processor: For the described hosted API use (transaction enrichment + anonymized analytics), Redwood is acting as a Processor on behalf of FinVera. Redwood processes data only on FinVera’s instructions and provides controls for deletion/export. Instances where Redwood would be a Controller are limited and would be explicitly documented in the contract (for example, where Redwood independently derives product-level analytics including identifiable attributes and sells aggregated insights to third parties).

2) SCC Module choice: We recommend SCC Module 2 (Processor-to-Processor) as the default for this engagement because FinVera will be sending PII to Redwood’s hosted API as part of customer-initiated calls. Module 2 best aligns with common hosted API flows and limits bilateral controller obligations. If FinVera wishes, we can also agree Module 3 in scenarios where joint decision-making over specific processing activities is required; that would require additional legal language around roles and responsibilities.

3) Retention / deletion: Default retention for hosted customers: cached KV/prefix caches are retained for up to 30 days; operational logs are retained for 90 days; model telemetry and aggregated metrics are retained in anonymized form for up to 24 months for product monitoring. Redwood supports subject access and deletion requests via an API and an outlined intake process; turnaround times are documented in Appendix A of the attached draft DPA. For Dedicated or Private deployments, retention windows and deletion controls are configurable and can be contractually specified.

Next steps proposed: legal-to-legal 30-minute sync to confirm Module 2 is acceptable and to review small DPA redlines. We can provide the full SOC 2 Type II on NDA prior to the call.

"

I flagged the following redlines in the DPA: subprocessor disclosure cadence (we propose quarterly updates), limitation on logging retention, and an explicit SLA for data deletion confirmations. I will attach suggested wording in a separate email to legal_ops for tracking.

If Ben is ok with that approach commercially, we should propose Thursday 3:30pm PST or Friday 11:00am PST as meeting options.
